chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Working with Roy Eldridge at Billy Berg's
summary: After a JATP tour, Young worked a few weeks at Berg's with Roy Eldridge, Anita O'Day, Willie Smith and Wardell Gray.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: This was in the '40's. '40. At that time I was playing with Roy Eldridge out at Billy Berg's. Me, Roy Eldridge -- Roy had the group -- Anita O'Day was singing with the group. And it's the only job I really ever worked with Roy, and the reason I worked that with him was we just came off a tour with Norman Granz Jazz at the Philharmonic. And he had a couple weeks out there. We worked it with him. Willie Willy Smith, Roy, myself, Wardell L. Gray, Jackie Mills on drums, Charlie Drayton on bass. He committed suicide later out in L.A. And Kennie Cursey on piano.

Yeah. I never forgot that. The front line was Wardell Gray, Willie Smith, Roy Eldridge, and myself. And the rhythm was Kennie Cursey on Piano, Jackie Mills on drums, and Charlie Drayton on the bass. And the singer was Anita O'Day.
Yeah, it was a groovy -- only two weeks, two or three weeks we were in that room there but --
That was Berg's on Vine Street?
That was Billy Berg's club on Vine Street?
You know Dottie Bigard told me that Billy Berg had four different clubs here which I --
This was the one -- I didn't know about any of his other clubs, but this one was the Vine Street club.
Yeah, that's the one I knew of.
Yeah, that's the only one I knew. But this was '40 -- I don't know what -- '45, '46. It was somewhere right around in there though.
